epics.title: Runtime foundations, reliable saves and first playable chapter
epics.description: Remove reliability blockers and establish contracts that let gameplay, content, art and QA advance independently.

epics.title: Creature collection, strategic combat and balanced progression
epics.description: Turn the basic encounter loop into a readable, varied system with individual companions, meaningful moves and a measured economy.

epics.title: Authored exploration, quests and a complete campaign
epics.description: Replace repeated terrain and hardcoded objectives with authored regions, NPCs, quests and an ending.

epics.title: Art, animation, audio and usable desktop/mobile play
epics.description: Deliver consistent pixel presentation and accessible, responsive controls, menus and performance.

epics.title: Testing, delivery and a supportable 1.0 release
epics.description: Make the game reproducibly buildable, tested, traceable, distributable and recoverable.

tasks.title: Define the 1.0 game design and measurable completion target
tasks.evidence: README.md describes a browser prototype; there is no design document, campaign target, content budget, or definition of a finished game.
scope: Document the recommended small single-player RPG: 3–5-hour first campaign, three distinctive regions with nine authored maps, 24 discoverable species/forms, six side quests, three shrine guardians and a final story resolution. These are planning targets to validate, not existing features.
Specify the exploration/capture/training/battle loop, failure rules, six-member active party plus reserve collection, move learning/evolution rules, and map/quest structure.
Set PC keyboard and mobile-touch support, offline-first local saves with export/import, and browser performance/accessibility budgets.

Identify stretch scope explicitly: no account backend, trading/PvP, monetization, native ports, or mandatory online services for 1.0. Preserve original art identity and eight-direction isometric movement.
accept: Versioned design, content inventory, success metrics and cut list live in docs/.
The first chapter can test all core mechanics; completing the campaign has an unambiguous ending.
Target platforms, party size, progression rules, and content counts are settled so downstream contracts can be written.
tasks.verify: Review each target against current mechanics and resource estimates; perform a short scope feasibility review and update the roadmap rather than silently expanding it.
tasks.parallel: Start immediately. Art reference gathering, audit reproduction, CI setup, and technical spikes can happen concurrently; final content implementation uses this baseline.

tasks.title: Prevent malformed saves from crashing startup and migrate to stable IDs
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:20–42 trusts nested team records; a v2 save with team={'0':7} reproduces "Cannot create property xp on number 7" and prevents window.mossvale from initializing. Species/regions are persisted as array indexes.
scope: Validate every save field, nested creature record, finite number, ID, progression flag, and position before constructing runtime state.
Introduce stable creature/region/entity IDs and an explicit schema version with tested v1/v2 migration before reordering content arrays.
Quarantine invalid payloads and retain a previous known-good checkpoint; do not silently overwrite an unsupported newer schema or erase recoverable progress.
Bound numeric fields, reconcile caught/seen/team consistency, and handle unavailable storage with a clear recovery path.
accept: The malformed nested-team fixture opens a playable recovery screen instead of crashing.
All known v1/v2 fixtures preserve collection, XP, inventory and unlocked regions; reordering definitions does not change their identities.
Truncated, invalid, future-version and storage-denied saves have documented safe outcomes; backup data survives a failed migration.
tasks.verify: Fixture tests for nested scalar/null records, extreme/NaN-like values, duplicate/unknown IDs, corrupted JSON, missing storage, future schemas and unchanged valid saves.
tasks.parallel: Begin the crash hotfix immediately without waiting for the architecture refactor. Agree stable-ID and save-envelope contracts with the architecture owner before the migration lands.

tasks.title: Split the monolithic runtime into modules with explicit data contracts
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js contains rendering, mutation, persistence, DOM menus, combat and content in one 282-line compressed IIFE; dist/style.css is seven very long lines. Shared mutable state makes independent edits conflict.
scope: Separate domain state, content definitions, world simulation, combat, save service, input, rendering, audio, and UI adapters into documented modules.
Define stable IDs, event payloads and state transitions; make domain logic independent of DOM/Canvas and inject RNG/time/storage.
Adopt readable formatting and a small build/dev workflow; keep Canvas unless a bounded engine spike proves a clear benefit.
Keep public gameplay behavior intact while migrating incrementally; gate mutable debug helpers to development/test builds.
accept: Modules have documented ownership and APIs; no domain module depends on querySelector or requestAnimationFrame.
Current behavior smoke tests pass during the split and old saves remain readable.
Gameplay/content/art/UI contributors can work in separate directories without simultaneously editing one runtime file.
tasks.verify: Run migration smoke tests, seeded capture/guardian flows and module-boundary checks on each incremental commit.
tasks.parallel: Architecture and save contracts need one coordinating owner. CI, art planning, story outlines and loader mitigation can run alongside; dependent implementations start after their specific contracts freeze.

tasks.title: Add reproducible development tooling and GitHub quality checks
tasks.evidence: The repository contains README plus dist assets only: no package manifest, lockfile, linter, formatter, committed tests or CI workflow. Earlier validation scripts exist only in the task workspace, not the repo.
scope: Provide one-command local development and checks, pinned tool versions and a lockfile.
Add formatting/linting, JavaScript syntax/build checks, content/asset reference validation, and a minimal browser smoke test.
Create a GitHub Actions workflow for pushes to main and branches; do not require PR approval or introduce mandatory merge gates contrary to the owner preference.
Document test commands and how to reproduce failures; keep tooling proportional to the game.
accept: A clean checkout installs reproducibly and runs the same checks locally and in GitHub Actions.
A deliberately broken asset reference or startup exception fails the relevant check.
main can receive direct commits while failed checks remain visible and actionable.
tasks.verify: Exercise the workflow with known-bad fixtures and verify a green run on the real default branch.
tasks.parallel: Start immediately; this is mostly isolated build configuration. Coordinate module paths with architecture; deeper tests can be added as systems stabilize.

tasks.title: Make encounters durable and handle pause, refresh and tab suspension
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:203–229 uses setTimeout for turns while battle state is not serialized. Browser reproduction: start capture, reload immediately; orbs drop 12→11 but the encounter disappears. document.hidden only stops loop rendering/simulation, not turn timers.
scope: Use explicit exploration, dialogue, battle, result and paused states with a single lifecycle controller.
Choose and implement a documented safe encounter checkpoint/resume policy so item consumption, HP, XP, captures and rewards commit exactly once.
Suspend or consistently resume animations/turn resolution on tab hiding, focus changes, refresh and browser back/forward; cancel stale callbacks.
Prevent double actions, menus over active turns, same-frame battle duplicates and orphan result transitions.
accept: Reloading at every capture/turn/reward boundary never loses an item without its corresponding action or duplicates a reward.
Pause/visibility behavior is deterministic and documented; stale callbacks cannot mutate a new encounter.
Exploration, dialogue, switch, defeat and result transitions all recover to a usable state.
tasks.verify: Seeded timer/checkpoint tests plus browser refresh/visibility tests at each transaction boundary, rapid keyboard/touch inputs and storage failures.
tasks.parallel: Needs state/save contracts. Can run alongside combat rule design and map authoring, but the combat implementation must integrate through this controller rather than adding independent timers.

tasks.title: Add a real loading state, asset validation and startup recovery
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:70 resolves both image.onload and image.onerror identically; aborting sprite8.png still boots with no failure message and an invisible player.
scope: Create a named asset manifest with sizes, expected frames and required/optional status.
Show load progress and a usable retry/error path; required missing player/map assets must not silently open normal play.
Provide deliberate fallbacks for optional assets, font/network failures and browser capability errors.
Validate assets at build time and distinguish cold loading from continuing a saved game.
accept: A missing required player sprite is detected, explained, and retryable; restoring the asset resumes play.
Optional audio/font failures do not break gameplay.
A cold start on a slow connection communicates progress and does not accept gameplay input before ready.
tasks.verify: Browser tests for 404, aborted requests, slow/throttled assets, decode failure and supported capability fallback.
tasks.parallel: Implement the immediate error path now. Migrate it to the final asset manifest with the architecture/art owners; tooling and presentation work can proceed independently.

tasks.title: Commit deterministic gameplay regression tests and fixtures
tasks.evidence: No tests are committed. Previous workspace browser scripts forced guardian HP to 1 and Math.random to 0, verifying wiring but not real difficulty, natural navigation or complete playability.
scope: Add pure-domain tests for movement/collision, capture probability, elemental effects, rewards, defeat, progression gates and save migrations.
Use injected seeded RNG/clock fixtures instead of mutating global Math.random or the live window.mossvale state in production.
Add browser flows for new game, real first capture, shrine unlock, region travel, shop, save/reload and touch input.
Cover exactly-once chest/reward behavior, invalid actions and frame-rate-independent movement; keep logic tests distinct from UI checks.
accept: Core regression tests run in CI and reproduce failures deterministically.
At least one first-chapter smoke flow wins using normal game actions without setting enemy HP.
Tests catch duplicate rewards, malformed saves, missing required assets and stale turn callbacks.
tasks.verify: Mutation-check a handful of critical rules to establish that tests detect the intended failures; retain failing seeds as fixtures.
tasks.parallel: QA can design scenarios immediately and implement against core contracts as they land. Do not let every system owner invent a separate incompatible test harness.

tasks.title: Create a data-driven map and event authoring pipeline
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:49–67 hardcodes one ellipse, central cross-path, pond, grass rules and the same special object positions for all regions. Terrain palettes change, but authored geography and event data do not exist.
scope: Define versioned map data for tiles, collision, elevations/layers, entity IDs, spawn points, interactables, portals, encounter zones and quest triggers.
Support a practical authoring workflow such as a constrained Tiled export or validated JSON with preview and documentation.
Validate references, portal pairs, spawn safety, objective reachability, missing assets and map bounds.
Separate static map data from persistent dynamic state; provide one migrated meadow map as a reference.
accept: A designer can change a route, encounter zone or event without editing simulation code.
Invalid maps fail validation with entity/path context.
The meadow reference map supports existing camp, chest, shrine and gate interactions using stable IDs.
tasks.verify: Schema fixtures, portal/reachability validation and a real authored-map smoke test.
tasks.parallel: Designers can sketch maps in parallel. Only schema/tool ownership is shared; separate map files become independent once the exporter contract is stable.

tasks.title: Make traversal, collisions, portals and camera reliable on every map
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:68 checks circular object radii; movement resolves X then Y and follows a fixed camera. resize resets user zoom. The follower uses a fixed offset regardless of obstacles or water.
scope: Implement tested eight-direction world movement with consistent world-space speed and collision shapes that match authored terrain/footprints.
Handle corner sliding, map boundaries, portal spawn direction, repeated interaction input, and stuck recovery.
Add camera bounds, sensible interpolation, persistent zoom, resize/orientation handling and robust occlusion.
Have followers use a movement history or safe path so they do not visually walk through obstacles or across ponds.
accept: Players can reach every required objective and portal without clipping or becoming trapped.
Movement distance is consistent across supported frame rates and opposite diagonals; all eight directions work on keyboard/touch.
Resize does not reset the chosen zoom; portal transitions preserve intended facing and place the party safely.
tasks.verify: Automated path/collision fixtures and hands-on traversal of every final map at 30/60/120Hz, narrow viewports and device rotation.
tasks.parallel: World simulation and map design can proceed on separate fixtures after the schema lands; camera/render integration must coordinate with animation and performance work.

tasks.title: Implement meaningful move sets, battle rules and status effects
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:203–225 offers one basic strike and one elemental move per species, unlimited elemental attacks, simple guard/potion/switch, and alternating enemy actions. Neutral elemental attack generally outdamages the basic move without a cost.
scope: Specify and implement a finite equipped move set with power, accuracy, resource/cooldown or opportunity-cost rules, targeting and turn ordering.
Add a small coherent status/stat-effect system and type matrix; avoid piling on mechanics before the first chapter is fun.
Centralize damage/capture/escape/item/switch resolution, legal actions and event output with seeded RNG.
Make battle UI, AI and simulations consume the same rule definitions; retain understandable capture feedback.
accept: At least three distinct useful combat choices exist in the first chapter; one unrestricted attack is not always the best option.
Effects have clear duration/stacking rules and recover correctly after switching, defeat, refresh or battle end.
All displayed chances and damage explanations match the actual rule engine.
tasks.verify: Rule fixtures for every effect, type matchup, legal action, turn order, damage boundary and resource cost; play a full early guardian encounter without debug intervention.
tasks.parallel: Battle rule design can begin with the spec. Implementation can run beside map/quest work once state/action contracts are frozen; AI and balancing depend on those rules.

tasks.title: Give trainers and shrine guardians deliberate battle behavior
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:220 selects the elemental move on odd turns and quick strike on even turns. Guardians reuse the same creature behavior with increased level/HP.
scope: Add bounded, deterministic AI policies that consider type matchup, health, resources, status and legal switches.
Create distinct guardian mechanics/telegraphs and encounter definitions for trainer teams; avoid hidden unavoidable punishments.
Provide adjustable difficulty/accessibility assistance rather than requiring grinding as the only solution.
Keep AI tunable via data and capture decision traces for balance diagnostics.
accept: Each of three guardians tests a different learned mechanic and has at least two viable player strategies.
AI never uses illegal actions or information it should not know; replayed seeds produce the same choices.
Early trainers teach mechanics and assistance options preserve campaign completion.
tasks.verify: AI scenario tests, seeded battle traces and human playtests with multiple team compositions.
tasks.parallel: AI authoring can share the battle engine with balance work; guardian scripts can be written independently per encounter after the action API and team model stabilize.

tasks.title: Model individual creatures, active party and reserve storage
tasks.evidence: save.caught is a species-index set and save.team is one record per species. Duplicate captures yield coins/XP and cannot become distinct companions; there is no limited active party or reserve collection.
scope: Separate discovered species from individual creature instances with stable IDs, level/XP, health, learned/equipped moves and optional nickname.
Implement the agreed six-member active party and reserve storage with reorder, swap and inspect actions.
Specify capture-at-capacity, duplicate capture, fainted party, active companion replacement and migration from one-per-species saves.
Avoid introducing random hidden traits unless the design has a clear purpose and UI explanation.
accept: Two captures of the same species can be distinct, persist correctly and be managed without losing either.
Party/reserve operations preserve identities, moves, XP and campaign flags across save/reload.
Full party, full storage and all-fainted edge cases have usable recovery paths.
tasks.verify: Instance identity/save fixtures and browser party/storage flows including capacity, duplicate capture and battle switching.
tasks.parallel: Agree instance/save contracts first. Collection UI, roster design and battle rules can then work concurrently against fixtures.

tasks.title: Build a bounded XP curve, move learning and evolution progression
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:43 and 133 use an unbounded linear level formula, fixed XP per outcome and HP increases. There are no learnsets, level cap or evolutions.
scope: Create an XP curve and level cap appropriate to the 3–5-hour campaign; define party XP distribution and avoid bench members becoming unusable.
Implement move-learning decisions, safe replacement and any agreed six evolution lines with explicit conditions and communication.
Apply HP/stat changes consistently for level/evolution, battle and storage; migrate existing experience without unreasonable boosts or loss.
Data-drive growth and evolution; integrate notifications into party and battle results.
accept: Progression unlocks meaningful choices throughout the campaign without mandatory repetitive grinding.
Learning/evolving preserves individual identity, valid moves, health ratios and saved state.
Cap, multi-level gains, declined evolution and old XP fixtures behave predictably.
tasks.verify: Progression fixture tests plus full-campaign level/XP traces and bench catch-up playtests.
tasks.parallel: Growth tables and learnsets can be designed alongside roster art; implementation integrates once collection and battle contracts are stable.

tasks.title: Author a coherent 24-species roster with roles and evolution lines
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:6–15 defines eight species that mainly differ by HP, type, sprite and one move. Species and region pools are embedded in code.
scope: Define 24 total discoverable species/forms, including the agreed evolution lines, without confusing forms with additional unique catches.
Give each a distinct combat role, habitat, encounter weight, growth/learnset and readable journal entry.
Keep region distribution intentional and ensure every required species is obtainable with no irreversible collection lockout.
Supply validated data and art briefs; implement a complete first-chapter subset before producing the remainder.
accept: The roster has explicit counts, roles, region availability and a discoverable completion plan.
No required species, evolution prerequisite or move references an undefined ID.
Species differentiation survives playtesting beyond merely swapping type/color.
tasks.verify: Content validation, encounter-availability checks and roster role review against the final battle rules.
tasks.parallel: Creature concepts/data and art briefs can run alongside map/story design. Final move/stat assignments need combat contracts; split production by stable species IDs.

tasks.title: Make encounters varied, paced and discoverable
tasks.evidence: dist/game.js:190–195 uses region-wide pools and a preference for unseen species; movement accumulates a grass-distance threshold. There are no zone-specific habitats, trainer events or encounter protection items.
scope: Author weighted encounter tables by map/zone with level ranges, rarity and clear habitat clues.
Define encounter grace periods, escape rules, trainer/one-time scripted encounters and optional suppression so exploration is not constantly interrupted.
Validate every campaign-required capture/evolution source and prevent scripted encounter reward duplication.
Communicate rarity/hints through the journal or NPCs instead of demanding blind random grinding.
accept: Routes feel different and required collection goals are achievable within the campaign pacing budget.
Encounter cooldowns/grace periods survive battle transitions and save/restore.
Scripted encounters trigger once as intended and random tables cover every required species.
tasks.verify: Seeded distribution tests, reachability/availability validation and timed exploration playtests.
tasks.parallel: Encounter table authoring can run per map alongside level design; implementation uses the shared event/battle interfaces.

tasks.title: Add a persistent quest, dialogue and world-event system
tasks.evidence: objective() derives one hardcoded step from captures/badges; Iris dialogue is repeated HTML. There are no branching dialogue nodes, persistent quest instances or general map events.
scope: Define quest objectives, prerequisite flags, rewards and completion transitions with stable IDs and once-only commits.
Build dialogue nodes with conditions, choices, event dispatch and NPC presentation; let content authors use validated data.
Support world changes after quests, objective markers, journal history and resumable interactions.
Keep a small expressive system; avoid building an unrestricted scripting language or editor before the chapter ships.
accept: A multi-step first-chapter quest can be authored without changing runtime code.
Dialogue/quest progress resumes after reload and rewards cannot be claimed twice.
Missing prerequisites, contradictory states and orphan references are caught by validation.
tasks.verify: Quest state transition fixtures and browser flows through branching dialogue, abort/restart, rewards and map changes.
tasks.parallel: Story writing can start now. Implementation needs map/save/event contracts; authors can build dialogue fixtures while the runtime is being completed.

tasks.title: Build nine authored maps with distinct exploration and secrets
tasks.evidence: All three existing regions reuse the same 25×25 terrain rules and camp/shrine/chest positions with different palettes and a few scenery sprites.
scope: Build the remaining six ridge/grove maps and refine the three meadow maps from the validated chapter, totaling nine authored maps.
Give each region distinctive geography, safe paths, landmarks, shortcuts, encounters and at least one meaningful exploration challenge.
Place NPCs, chests, quest events, portals and shrine approaches using validated map data.
Stage production: complete and playtest one region first, then build ridge and grove from proven authoring patterns.
accept: Players can distinguish regions by layout and activities, not just recoloring.
Every main objective and all six side-quest paths are reachable on keyboard/touch without sequence-break softlocks.
Each map passes reference, collision, spawn, portal and event validation.
tasks.verify: Full navigation walkthroughs from new and mid-campaign saves, secret discovery playtests and map validation in CI.
tasks.parallel: Design all regions concurrently after the schema is stable; implement separate map files in parallel. Do not duplicate the unproven first chapter before its playtest gate.

tasks.title: Deliver the first-play tutorial, campaign story and satisfying ending
tasks.evidence: The current game starts immediately in the meadow and ends with a guardian result message plus objective text. There is no playable introduction, narrative arc, final sequence or credits.
scope: Write a concise story grounded in the three shrines, Iris and the companions; introduce region NPCs and motivations.
Teach movement, interaction, capture, type strengths, switching, healing and shrine progression through play with skip/review options.
Integrate three region chapters and a final resolution using the quest/event engine; make the next goal consistently discoverable.
Add ending/credits and a persisted completion state that lets players continue unfinished exploration.
accept: A new player can reach the first capture and shrine without reading the external README.
The campaign has an identifiable beginning, escalating middle and explicit final resolution.
Returning or completing players receive correct objectives and can continue collecting without losing progress.
tasks.verify: Blind first-time-player sessions and uninterrupted full campaign walkthroughs, including skipping tutorial and replaying ending from a checkpoint.
tasks.parallel: Writing and tutorial storyboards start after the spec; integration proceeds per chapter against map/quest/AI fixtures, not all at the end.

tasks.title: Add six side quests, regional secrets and collection goals
tasks.evidence: The prototype has one reusable objective chain and one treasure chest per region. There are no side quests or exploration consequences.
scope: Create two authored side quests per region with different activities: exploration, creature observation/training, NPC help or a small battle puzzle.
Give rewards and world/dialogue consequences, not only more coins; integrate regional secrets with journal clues.
Design completionist tracking and fallback access so optional paths do not permanently lock a required creature or reward.
Document prerequisites and quest graph for validation and QA.
accept: All six quests have clear starts, objectives, rewards and completion states.
Optional content complements the main campaign and can be finished after the ending.
Rewards commit once, and no side quest can block mandatory progression.
tasks.verify: Quest graph validation and playthroughs in different main/side-quest orders with save/reload at each step.
tasks.parallel: Each quest can be authored independently once quest/map/collection contracts are available; reserve one integration owner for global reward/flag consistency.

tasks.title: Create a coherent inventory, shop and reward economy
tasks.evidence: Inventory is three scalar counts. Iris restores health and fills orbs to 12 for free; duplicate catches grant 10 coins; shops have hardcoded prices and two items. These choices have not been economy-tested.
scope: Specify free-recovery and refill policy intentionally; prevent the campaign from requiring coin grinding or becoming unwinnable after spending supplies.
Define data-driven item types, quantities, effects, prices and reward tables with transactional purchase/use logic.
Add inventory inspection/use and clear insufficient-funds/capacity feedback; retain convenient camp recovery.
Balance reward sources and sinks, duplicate captures, chest rewards and guardian rewards against expected route length.
accept: Every supported save can recover to a playable state without needing paid services or consumable luck.
Purchases, item use and rewards are once-only and capacity-safe across save/restore.
Expected campaign spending/rewards are documented with normal and low-skill routes.
tasks.verify: Transaction/capacity fixtures and an economy simulation plus human low-resource playthroughs.
tasks.parallel: Economy tables can be drafted alongside battle design. Transaction code must share the durable action/save service rather than implementing separate mutations.

tasks.title: Measure and tune natural campaign difficulty and pacing
tasks.evidence: Previous tests verify unlock wiring by forcing enemy HP to 1. No natural campaign duration, guardian difficulty, capture time, collection odds or viable team composition has been measured.
scope: Build seeded batch simulations for combat, capture/collection availability, XP curves and economy using the real rules.
Run blind human sessions for first-time, casual and experienced players; record time-to-first-capture, shrine attempts, grind time and completion time.
Tune numbers, encounters, AI and tutorial feedback so multiple teams/strategies succeed.
Set explicit acceptance budgets and retain difficult/failing seeds plus playtest notes for future regression.
accept: The target 3–5-hour campaign is supported by measured sessions rather than assumed from content count.
Every guardian has multiple viable strategies and no required action demands repetitive grind beyond the agreed budget.
Capture completion, failure recovery and economy are viable for low-resource and unlucky routes.
tasks.verify: Publish simulation summaries and anonymized playtest observations; rerun key seeds after every balance change.
tasks.parallel: Simulation tools can start as battle rules stabilize; final tuning must follow integrated content. Avoid parallel authors changing global balance tables without a coordinating designer.

tasks.title: Add a title/continue flow and persistent player settings
tasks.evidence: index.html opens straight into play; there is no title/new-game/continue flow. Sound starts off each time, zoom resets on resize, and other settings do not persist.
scope: Create game-native new/continue and settings flows that lead promptly into play; make destructive restart explicit and recoverable.
Persist audio volume/mute, text speed, motion preferences, control sensitivity/run behavior and zoom where supported.
Provide consistent pause/settings access during exploration and appropriate restrictions during durable battle transactions.
Represent save/storage errors and finished-game continuation clearly.
accept: Fresh, existing, completed and invalid-save states each have an intentional entry flow.
Settings persist and do not overwrite game progress; reset never silently destroys the only save.
Menus are usable on keyboard, touch, narrow screens and 200% text enlargement.
tasks.verify: Browser flows for first launch, continue, new game, settings persistence, denied storage and restart recovery.
tasks.parallel: UI layouts can be designed immediately; implementation depends only on entry/save/state contracts, allowing it to run beside content work.

tasks.title: Add save slots, portable backups and recovery tools
tasks.evidence: The only save is localStorage on one browser origin. There is no export/import, checkpoint restore, named slot or user recovery; hosted and localhost progress cannot transfer.
scope: Implement the agreed small number of slots with timestamps, progress summaries and safe overwrite/delete confirmation.
Add validated export/import with schema/version checks, size limits, preview and rollback to the prior save.
Offer restore-from-backup and explain local-only storage/device/origin boundaries in player-facing language.
Do not add accounts/cloud sync to solve backup needs for the offline-first 1.0 target.
accept: A player can export on one supported browser and import on another with identical progression.
Invalid/future-version imports never overwrite valid progress; interrupted writes leave a usable backup.
Slot switching, new game and recovery are accessible without devtools.
tasks.verify: Round-trip fixtures across v1/v2/current schemas, storage-denied/quota scenarios and cross-browser file import/export checks.
tasks.parallel: Work can run independently of map/combat content after stable save/instance contracts; coordinate UI with entry menus and accessibility.

tasks.title: Improve exploration, battle, party and journal information design
tasks.evidence: Menus replace modal.innerHTML and reset focus/scroll on every battle render. The journal exposes only a simple species filter, and map/objective cues are rudimentary.
scope: Create cohesive HUD/menu patterns for objective history, waypoint/map clues, inventory, individual creatures, equipped moves and reserve storage.
Keep battle choices, type information, turn history, status and resource costs legible without overwhelming mobile screens.
Preserve focus/scroll and selection when state updates; expose hidden/unknown species clues without spoiling content.
Support text expansion, user settings and input modes without duplicating state in UI code.
accept: Players can find the next objective, explain why an action is effective, and manage their team without external instructions.
Battle updates do not unexpectedly lose keyboard focus or scroll a chosen control away.
Core screens remain usable at narrow widths and enlarged text with consistent navigation/back behavior.
tasks.verify: Task-based usability sessions plus keyboard/touch and text-zoom screen checks using real final content.
tasks.parallel: Design can run in parallel immediately; UI implementation uses shared domain contracts. Divide screen ownership but keep navigation/focus primitives under one owner.

tasks.title: Make the game accessible across input, motion, color and text needs
tasks.evidence: The prototype has labels, a dialog role and basic focus wrapping, but world objectives are Canvas-only and battle actions rebuild DOM. Small text and motion/audio behavior have not been systematically audited.
scope: Provide reliable keyboard-only controls, focus restoration, visible focus, logical reading order and inert background while dialogs are open.
Add text-based nearby-interaction/objective/map cues, non-color type/status indicators and appropriate live announcements.
Honor reduced motion, text speed, audio volume and 200% text enlargement; adjust contrast and minimum touch targets.
Document practical screen-reader support and limitations honestly; do not claim a fully accessible spatial world without testing it.
accept: Keyboard-only players can complete all menu/battle/interact flows without focus traps or hidden controls.
Important state is not conveyed only by color, sound or animation.
Representative screen-reader, motion-disabled and 200%-text tasks pass with documented remaining constraints.
tasks.verify: Automated UI accessibility checks plus manual VoiceOver/NVDA-style testing, keyboard walkthroughs and color/motion/text audits.
tasks.parallel: Audit and design guidance should start early; final acceptance follows integrated HUD/input screens. Many fixes can be scoped per UI module without blocking content authors.

tasks.title: Harden touch input, orientation and browser compatibility
tasks.evidence: Touch uses pointer capture and a button grid; mobile dialogs are fixed overlays. Prior workspace checks used desktop Chromium emulation, not physical iOS Safari/Android devices.
scope: Define a supported desktop Chrome/Firefox/Safari and iOS Safari/Android Chrome matrix; test real devices as well as emulation.
Handle safe areas, browser bars, rotation, pointer cancellation/multi-touch, accidental page scroll and background resumption.
Adjust control layout/target sizes and audio unlocking for mobile; verify small screens and landscape orientation.
Persist chosen input/run behavior and ensure hidden/stuck pointers cannot keep a character moving.
accept: A complete first chapter works on target physical mobile devices with no inaccessible buttons or stuck movement.
Rotation and browser chrome changes retain game/menu state and do not reset zoom/settings unexpectedly.
All supported browsers load, save and recover as documented; unsupported features have a clear fallback.
tasks.verify: Record device/OS/browser versions and manual scenario results, including 320px widths, landscape and interruption during battle.
tasks.parallel: Device matrix planning and input testing start early; final fixes integrate after HUD/lifecycle contracts. Platform investigations can be split by browser/device.

tasks.title: Profile and optimize rendering, asset delivery and battery use
tasks.evidence: drawWorld recomputes terrain details and sorts objects every frame, draws large cropped PNGs and applies Canvas filters. Minimap also redraws frequently; there are no performance measurements or budgets.
scope: Instrument frame time, startup/asset load and memory on agreed desktop and representative mobile hardware.
Cache static terrain, sort only changing depth entries, bake repeated tints/size variants where measured useful and avoid unnecessary DOM/save work.
Optimize atlases/asset dimensions and delivery with a manifest; set a documented pixel/DPR strategy and quality tiers.
Throttle or stop background work properly and retain crisp pixel art while reducing mobile battery load.
accept: Meet documented budgets such as desktop 60fps and mobile 30fps minimum, with representative p95 frame times and bounded memory growth.
Cold start and compressed transfer budgets are measured on a stated connection/device; required content loads reliably.
Thirty-minute sessions and repeated travel/menu transitions do not show a growing memory/resource leak.
tasks.verify: Profile real devices and browser traces; compare before/after metrics on final maps with dense scenery, VFX and UI.
tasks.parallel: Baseline instrumentation can start early. Optimize once representative content exists; do not concurrently rewrite renderer APIs while animation/asset integration depends on them.

tasks.title: Produce eight-direction movement and creature animation sets
tasks.evidence: The player has four static directions selected in movement(); diagonal movement reuses left/right. Walking only bobs sprites, and the follower is a fixed offset.
scope: Create consistent eight-direction player idle/walk/run sets with frame timing, foot anchors and draw-depth rules.
Define a realistic creature animation budget: idle/walk/battle actions/hit/faint/capture for campaign roster, with controlled reusable patterns.
Integrate animations through a renderer-independent state/event contract and motion preference settings.
Validate atlas frames/pivots and transitions so pixel scale and contact points remain consistent.
accept: All eight travel directions have intentional readable animation rather than four still images and bobbing.
Player, followers and battle creatures keep stable feet/pivots through transitions with no clipping.
Animation timing does not affect simulation results; reduced-motion mode remains understandable.
tasks.verify: Atlas validation, animation contact sheets and hands-on walking/battle checks in all directions and supported viewports.
tasks.parallel: Animation briefs/rig conventions can start with art standards. Artists can split by player/species once shared anchors and frame conventions are fixed; runtime integration has one owner.

tasks.title: Create a consistent art pipeline and full campaign asset inventory
tasks.evidence: The repo has 24 independently cropped PNG sprites from generated sheets, including eight creatures and a handful of landmarks. There is no source atlas metadata, environment tile set, interiors or systematic asset budget.
scope: Set pixel resolution, palette, isometric angle, lighting, scale, silhouettes, anchors and transparency standards.
Create the full asset inventory for 24 species/forms, NPCs, region terrain, hub/interior/dungeon props, shrine/battle backgrounds and UI icons.
Store source/atlas metadata and deterministic export tools; fix crop-edge fragments and inconsistent scales.
Produce first-chapter assets first, then complete remaining region batches; log provenance for the rights audit.
accept: Every 1.0 content asset has an owner/status, stable manifest ID and validated dimensions/pivot.
The same player/creature/environment assets look consistent in exploration, menus and battle.
Production exports can be regenerated without hand-cropping undocumented sheets.
tasks.verify: Asset/reference CI, pixel-art review, representative scene comparisons and transparency/anchor contact sheets.
tasks.parallel: Art conventions and briefs can begin immediately. Production is parallel by region/species after roster/map contracts, with one art-direction review to avoid incompatible batches.

tasks.title: Add music, ambience and readable gameplay sound design
tasks.evidence: tone() creates a short triangle oscillator beep. There is no music, ambience, differentiated creature/action sound, mixer or persisted volume.
scope: Create a small licensed/original score for regions, battles, guardians and ending plus ambient loops and action/UI cues.
Implement master/music/SFX controls, crossfades and lifecycle-safe playback with browser user-gesture unlocking.
Use distinct sound feedback for hits, elemental moves, capture states, rewards and danger without making audio essential to understanding.
Track provenance and optimize formats/loading; recover gracefully when audio is unavailable.
accept: Region/battle transitions sound cohesive and do not leak or layer duplicate audio loops.
Volume/mute persists, mobile audio starts only after a valid gesture, and hidden/pause behavior is intentional.
All important sound cues also have clear visual/text equivalents.
tasks.verify: Playback interruption/transition tests and headphone/speaker/mobile listening review; verify final license inventory.
tasks.parallel: Composition and SFX production can run independently from map/combat implementation after briefs; runtime mixer integration needs lifecycle/settings events.

tasks.title: Run a release-quality campaign, save and platform QA program
tasks.evidence: There is no committed test plan, supported device matrix or defect triage process. Prior automated paths exercise a subset of the prototype and are not a full natural playthrough.
scope: Create a test matrix covering every main/side quest, creature/evolution availability, party capacity, item transaction, map portal and ending.
Exercise new/mid/old/completed/corrupt saves, migration, refresh/suspension, denied storage and replay/backtracking orders.
Run natural full campaigns on target devices; organize external playtests and classify defects by severity and reproducible seed/save.
Establish release thresholds: no startup/data-loss/softlock defects and no unresolved critical platform failures.
accept: A versioned QA matrix and reproducible defect log are maintained throughout production.
Every required content path and migration/platform combination has recorded results before release.
Release blockers are fixed or explicitly cut with a safe player outcome; gameplay difficulty is tested without forced HP/cheats.
tasks.verify: Independent full-campaign playthroughs, fixture regressions and cross-device tests against the candidate build.
tasks.parallel: Test design and exploratory testing begin immediately. Final campaign/platform sign-off waits for all 1.0 systems/content; QA is a continuous lane, not a last-week task.

tasks.title: Document code, artwork, audio and font rights for distribution
tasks.evidence: The repository has no LICENSE or credits/provenance file. PNG artwork was generated and fonts are imported from Google Fonts; reusable asset/source terms have not been recorded.
scope: Inventory code dependencies, fonts, artwork sources, generated assets and music/SFX with provenance and distribution terms.
Choose and document intended code/assets licensing separately, preserving third-party notices and attribution requirements.
Add credits/attribution and replace anything whose release rights cannot be established.
Make this a focused distribution review, not a speculative requirement for legal services or monetization.
accept: Release includes clear code/asset licensing, complete credits and required third-party notices.
Each shipped asset has a recorded source/provenance and usable distribution basis.
No undocumented placeholder audio/art dependency remains.
tasks.verify: Review inventory against the packaged build, dependency licenses and title/ending credits.
tasks.parallel: Inventory preparation starts immediately and can run alongside production; final verification depends on the actual final art/audio/package.

tasks.title: Make GitHub main the documented release source and automate verified delivery
tasks.evidence: GitHub contains a snapshot imported from the separately hosted Sites source repository. No workflow currently builds/publishes from GitHub, and the README link alone does not make commits deploy automatically.
scope: Document the source-of-truth and publishing relationship between GitHub main and the existing Sites deployment; avoid silently changing hosting provider or audience.
Create a deterministic static build/package pipeline, preview/staging process and a secure supported publish mechanism or documented release handoff.
Embed build/version identity, validate base paths/assets/cache headers, and ensure a save-safe update strategy.
Provide rollback instructions and preserve old save compatibility; direct main commits remain allowed as requested.
accept: A known GitHub commit produces a reproducible artifact, and the deployed build can be traced to that commit.
Preview, publish and rollback steps are tested with supported permissions; no secrets are stored in source.
Updating the live game preserves audience and valid existing saves, with no accidental assumption that GitHub push already deploys.
tasks.verify: Exercise a non-production preview/release artifact plus a controlled publish/rollback; verify asset paths and embedded build identity.
tasks.parallel: Can run beside gameplay/content once CI and packaging are stable. One release owner must coordinate publishing permissions/source identity; do not let separate workers independently deploy.

tasks.title: Add bounded diagnostics, feedback and support information
tasks.evidence: Startup/storage exceptions are mostly swallowed; there is no build ID, error report, reproducible player diagnostic export or support entry beyond the GitHub repository.
scope: Expose version/build ID, a bounded local error/event log and a user-triggered diagnostic export with sensitive save details omitted by default.
Add a clear issue/feedback path and bug-report template capturing browser, device, steps, version and optional repro save consent.
Record failed asset/save/transaction states locally for troubleshooting without requiring mandatory telemetry or a backend.
Document limitations, known issues and recovery steps; use opt-in analytics only if later justified separately.
accept: A tester can report a reproducible error tied to a release version without sharing unnecessary personal/local data.
Diagnostics do not grow indefinitely or affect play/performance; unsupported storage still has a visible support path.
Bug-report/recovery instructions are reachable in-game and in repository docs.
tasks.verify: Trigger known asset/save errors, export diagnostics and verify privacy/bounds/version attribution.
tasks.parallel: Issue templates/documentation can start immediately; runtime diagnostics integrate after lifecycle/save/build contracts. Independent of narrative/art production.

tasks.title: Ship a verified 1.0 candidate, credits, release notes and rollback plan
tasks.evidence: There are no releases, release checklist, content completeness criteria or proven rollback/migration matrix in the repository.
scope: Audit every 1.0 issue against the agreed design and explicitly defer optional work; complete content, credits and player documentation.
Prepare a tagged candidate with changelog, save/version compatibility notes and tested artifacts.
Run the final clean-checkout, full-campaign, device, accessibility, asset/rights and migration gates.
Publish using the established hosting mechanism and record rollback/recovery steps plus any known nonblocking issues.
accept: All 1.0 blocking issue criteria pass; no unresolved crash, data-loss, softlock or required-content defect remains.
The playable release is traceable to a GitHub tag/commit and has accurate credits/release notes.
Rollback is possible without making valid player saves unreadable or changing access permissions.
tasks.verify: Release checklist signed off with actual evidence links, clean-install test, campaign completion and rollback rehearsal.
tasks.parallel: Checklist/release-note preparation can happen early; final packaging and deployment are sequential after the candidate passes all release gates.

tasks.title: Prove a complete first chapter before scaling the campaign
tasks.evidence: Current tests establish separate prototype flows, but no authored chapter combines tutorial, quests, normal battles, reliable saves and a measured guardian into a validated player experience.
scope: Deliver the first three meadow hub/route/shrine maps, an eight-species starter subset, a short playable tutorial/quest chain and a meaningful guardian using the agreed core contracts.
Run the chapter from new game through its natural guardian win with normal actions, including capture, party decisions, healing, travel and interrupted-save recovery.
Use temporary but valid art/audio where necessary; record interaction, pacing and usability evidence before duplicating the loop into the remaining regions.
Feed findings back into the design, battle, map and quest contracts; explicitly freeze or revise them before bulk content production.
accept: First-time testers can complete the chapter with understandable goals and no debug HP/RNG manipulation.
There are no startup, save-loss, progression-softlock or required-path failures in the chapter.
A checkpoint review records what is proven, unresolved issues, scope cuts and whether bulk production can start.
tasks.verify: Run at least three blind first-time-player sessions plus deterministic normal-action regression flows; record time, attempts, confusion points and migration/interruption outcomes.
tasks.parallel: First-chapter content, art placeholders and UI can be integrated in parallel once the core contracts exist. This is a sequential validation gate before the remaining map/campaign production; it does not wait for the full roster, final audio or all nine maps.

tasks.title: Evaluate opt-in cloud saves and cross-device accounts
scope: Assess player demand, hosting/authentication/storage costs and account recovery.
Define secure identity, save conflict resolution, offline synchronization, privacy/deletion and version compatibility before adding a backend.
Keep local play/export/import available without an account.
accept: A written go/no-go and threat/cost model precede implementation.
If pursued, offline/cloud conflicts, device loss and account deletion have tested outcomes.

tasks.title: Evaluate trading or PvP as a separate online product track
scope: Choose trading OR synchronous/asynchronous PvP through a separate design/prototype; do not assume both are cheap additions.
Specify authoritative server validation, creature ownership, matchmaking/consistency, disconnect recovery, abuse controls and operational budget.
Prevent manipulated local/debug state from becoming trusted online inventory or competitive outcomes.
accept: A scoped online prototype proves state authority and reconnect behavior before production commitment.
Costs, privacy, abuse handling and ongoing operations have explicit owners.

tasks.title: Expand postgame with rematches, challenge routes and new regions
scope: Use completion/playtest feedback to select rematches, challenge rules or one additional region rather than adding all at once.
Reuse validated map/quest/roster pipelines and set a separate content/reward budget.
Maintain existing save compatibility and avoid invalidating completed players’ collections.
accept: The expansion has its own measurable scope, estimate and compatibility plan.
A replayable challenge prototype demonstrates meaningful variation before broad content production.

tasks.title: Evaluate installable offline play and safe service-worker updates
scope: Assess demand for PWA/offline installation across supported browsers.
Design versioned asset caches, offline font/audio support, update notices and rollback without mixed-version saves/assets.
Keep the standard browser route working when service workers or installation are unsupported.
accept: A prototype proves offline startup and save-safe updates on target devices.
Stale/mixed caches, failed updates and storage pressure have explicit recovery tests.

tasks.title: Evaluate translations, controller input and additional platform ports
scope: Prioritize one expansion at a time based on player demand: translation infrastructure, gamepad support or a specific native wrapper.
Separate content strings and validate layout/input/platform requirements without rewriting game rules.
Estimate QA/distribution/support costs for each target before committing to it.
accept: Each selected target has a separate scope, compatibility matrix and cost estimate.
A localized/input/port prototype passes existing gameplay and save regressions.
